"On the Air," featured David Rubinoff, violinist and orchestra leader who appeared with Eddie Cantor on the radio and in theatres during the 1930's and 40's. How formal everyone dressed in the studio,probably to give the place a touch of class. The explanation of how radio waves worked was nicely done. Historically very interesting and entertaining.

There's an awful lot of padding in this 10-minute short. About a third is taken up watching an orchestra play and listening to the ridiculously-serious Westbrook Van Voorhis (using his Hugh Conrad moniker) bellow his intoned introductions. He even thrusts his finger to cue Rubinoff, which would be the director's job on a real radio programme. Finally, the usual Jam Handy voice-over guy shows up to tell us about how broadcast sounds are made and go from the studio to the home. Some animation here. There are nice close-up shots of carbon and ribbon mikes of the 1930s.

You know what they say about guys with big feet..
What do they say? We don't find out, as this story ends way before we find out. We DO find out the soldier has size 16 (!!) feet, and has to wear sandals? What does happen? Oh the suspense!
Pity the film ran short, it would have been interesting to know if they managed to kit him out?
This is only a portion of the original news reel. I would have given it five stars if the whole reel was included.
